question: Can supervised within-class attraction, implemented through Newtonian-inspired or relativity-inspired update rules on the input space or a three-dimensional PCA projection, contract class variance enough to create more discriminative data for a later dimensionality-reduction method?

key_findings.claim: GDR is a supervised, label-conditioned data-contraction preprocessor rather than a complete learned dimensionality-reduction map.
key_findings.evidence: The algorithm separates points by class and repeatedly moves every point toward other points with the same label. The relativity variant first projects all data to three PCA coordinates and later reconstructs those coordinates to the original feature dimension; the paper then says a separate dimensionality-reduction method may be applied to the transformed data. Thus its distinctive operation changes training samples but neither chooses a final embedding dimension nor learns an explicit out-of-sample function.

anchors.section: 3 Gravitational Dimensionality Reduction and 3.1 Projection onto 3D Space Manifold

key_findings.claim: The Newtonian update cancels its own inverse-distance factor, so each distinct pair contributes a unit-length step rather than a Newtonian distance-dependent displacement.
key_findings.evidence: Equations 12-13 define the scalar movement as 1/r_ij and multiply it by the unnormalized vector x_i-x_j, whose norm is r_ij. Consequently ||(x_i-x_j)/r_ij||=1 for every noncoincident pair. The full point update sums these unit vectors without a learning rate, time step, mass, damping term, or normalization by class size; the inverse-square force therefore does not survive in the implemented displacement magnitude.

key_findings.claim: The relativity variant does not compute geodesics or a data-dependent spacetime geometry despite repeatedly describing its updates as geodesic motion.
key_findings.evidence: The method declares a three-dimensional PCA subspace to be a space manifold, freezes time, sets G=M=c=1, and inserts a Schwarzschild or Minkowski metric around each currently processed data point. It does not specify a stress-energy tensor, solve Einstein's field equations for the dataset, calculate Christoffel symbols, solve a geodesic equation, or integrate a geodesic. Instead it equates a scalar movement budget with diagonal metric terms and directly adds independently chosen coordinate increments. A metric's local line element alone does not make those coordinate-wise increments a shortest path.

anchors.section: 3.4 Relativity Gravitation Algorithm and 3.4.1 Using Schwarzschild Metric

key_findings.claim: The Schwarzschild update is scale-dependent and mathematically undefined at ordinary locations in the arbitrary PCA coordinate system.
key_findings.evidence: With G=M=c=1, g_rr=(1-2/r)^-1 is singular at r=2 and negative for r<2, making the paper's real square root of a positive movement divided by g_rr undefined. The angular terms r^2 and r^2 sin^2(theta) also vanish at r=0 or on a polar axis. Because PCA coordinates have no physical units and may be rescaled without changing the underlying classification problem, the arbitrary value r=2 can be crossed merely by changing feature scale. The paper provides no nondimensionalization, epsilon, branch handling, singularity treatment, or invariance test.

key_findings.claim: The Minkowski rule is not directed toward the attracting point in Cartesian space.
key_findings.evidence: For g_xx=g_yy=g_zz=1, Equations 27-29 make every component of the pair update negative, with magnitude sqrt(alpha_k/r_ij). No factor encodes the sign or Cartesian direction of x_i-x_j. The update therefore moves x_j along the global negative coordinate directions regardless of where x_i lies, which is coordinate drift rather than attraction. The paper's own Figure 2 says this variant works only up to some point but does not diagnose the directional defect.

anchors.section: 4.4 GDR with Relativity Gravitation Using the Minkowski Metric

key_findings.claim: The empirical evidence consists of one in-sample digits visualization and does not support the conclusion's claim of extensive quantitative comparison.
key_findings.evidence: All experiments use the 1,797-sample, 64-feature scikit-learn digits dataset. Figures show six iterations of colored 3D PCA scatterplots and separately recomputed 2D t-SNE views for Newtonian, Schwarzschild, Minkowski, and coordinate-weight variants. There is no numeric table, classification accuracy, held-out split, trustworthiness or continuity score, intra/inter-class statistic, runtime, memory result, uncertainty, seed count, hypothesis test, or competing dimensionality-reduction baseline. The conclusion nevertheless calls the experiments extensive and both quantitative and qualitative.

key_findings.claim: The paper explicitly lacks an out-of-sample transform, so its figures cannot establish supervised generalization.
key_findings.evidence: The authors state that the current GDR algorithm does not support test data not used during training. Since every movement requires the labels and current positions of other same-class samples, simply processing held-out points would either require held-out labels or a new inductive extension. Visual separation of the same labeled samples used to construct the transformation is therefore expected from the objective and is not evidence that unseen examples become easier to classify.

anchors.section: 3.2 Sorting Based on Density and 3.3 Newtonian Gravitation Algorithm

key_findings.claim: Convergence, stability, scaling, and causal component value are left unvalidated.
key_findings.evidence: Algorithm 1 says to iterate until convergence but defines neither an objective nor a stopping condition, monotonicity result, or stability bound. Each iteration considers essentially every ordered pair within each class, giving quadratic within-class interaction work before plotting and density processing. The experiments show only six visual iterations and do not ablate density sorting, PCA, class-size normalization, coordinate weights beyond three extremes, or the physics-inspired rules against simpler centroid contraction and metric-learning objectives.

anchors.section: 3.2 Sorting Based on Density and 3.3 Newtonian Gravitation Algorithm

key_findings.claim: The released implementation confirms several paper-level reproducibility hazards rather than resolving them.
key_findings.evidence: The author repository's latest commit inspected for this review replaces the undefined convergence test with a fixed iteration count, uses the unit-step Newtonian formula verbatim, and suppresses Schwarzschild radial movement whenever g_rr is nonpositive while leaving other angular singularities exposed. It also assumes integer class labels contiguous from zero and applies ten-neighbor LOF separately within each class. These operational choices are not reported or tested in the paper and can materially change behavior on small, imbalanced, differently encoded, or rescaled datasets.

method.core_idea: Contract labeled samples within each class through repeated pairwise attraction, optionally in a three-dimensional PCA space, so a later embedding method displays more separated classes.
method.mechanism: Samples are split by label and sorted within each class using Local Outlier Factor. In the Newtonian branch, each target point receives the sum of normalized vectors pointing toward every other same-class point. In the relativity branch, data are projected to three PCA coordinates; each pair defines a local spherical or Cartesian coordinate system, scalar movement 1/r is split by three alpha weights, and coordinate increments are derived from diagonal Schwarzschild or Minkowski coefficients. Samples are processed sequentially, so earlier moves affect later ones. The three-dimensional data are inverse-transformed to the input dimension, after which a separate DR method may be run.
assumptions: Reducing within-class variance is desirable even when it destroys meaningful within-class modes and local neighborhoods.
All labels used during contraction are correct, available, and appropriate for the downstream question.
A three-dimensional PCA projection can be treated as a physical spatial manifold without estimating data geometry or curvature.
Freezing time preserves enough of the claimed relativity mechanism to justify a spacetime interpretation.
Setting G, M, and c to one is meaningful for arbitrary, unit-free PCA coordinates.
A metric line element can be converted into a geodesic step by independently allocating scalar movement across coordinates.
The Schwarzschild coordinate singularities and the r<2 region will not invalidate real-valued updates.
Sequential, order-dependent movement is made robust by a single LOF-derived ordering.
Unit pairwise Newtonian steps remain stable across class sizes, feature scales, densities, and iteration counts.
Visual separation under t-SNE reflects improved transferable discrimination rather than label-conditioned training-sample collapse.
Reconstructing a three-coordinate PCA representation into d dimensions is useful before applying another DR algorithm.
An inductive out-of-sample rule can eventually be added without changing the essential algorithm.

techniques.role: Uses class labels to move samples only toward other samples in the same class.
Processes high-density representatives before or after low-density points according to a fixed importance order.
Implements the Newtonian branch as a sum of normalized same-class direction vectors.
Provides the three coordinates required by the relativity-inspired branch.
Allocates movement across radial, polar, and azimuthal coordinates using diagonal Schwarzschild coefficients.
Allocates movement across three Cartesian coordinates under a flat diagonal metric.
Updates points in place so processed locations influence subsequent pair interactions.
Returns the three-coordinate result to the original feature dimension for visualization or later DR.

evaluations.setting: Scikit-learn digits data with 1,797 samples, 64 input features, and ten labels
evaluations.metric: Visual class separation across six displayed iterations in 3D PCA views and 2D t-SNE views
evaluations.result: The shown training samples form increasingly compact color-coded groups for Newtonian updates with and without PCA and for the Schwarzschild variant
evaluations.baseline: The unmodified data at iteration zero; no competing supervised DR or metric-learning method

evaluations.setting: Relativity-inspired GDR with the Minkowski metric and alpha_x=alpha_y=alpha_z=0.33
evaluations.result: The paper reports that the variant works only up to some point and is visually weaker than Schwarzschild GDR
evaluations.baseline: Qualitative comparison to the paper's Schwarzschild plots

evaluations.setting: Schwarzschild GDR with three extreme coordinate-weight settings
evaluations.metric: Visual 3D PCA and t-SNE progression for radial-only, polar-only, and azimuthal-only movement
evaluations.result: The radial-only setting visually contracts classes most strongly; no numeric embedding-quality or predictive metric is reported
evaluations.baseline: The three coordinate-weight extremes compared only by plotted appearance

limitations: Author-stated: the proposed algorithm is supervised; an unsupervised version is future work.
Author-stated: the current method does not support unseen out-of-sample test data.
Author-stated: other cosmological metric tensors and gravitational waves are left to future work.
Reviewer-identified: GDR's distinctive operation is sample transformation, while final dimensionality reduction is delegated to PCA or another method.
Reviewer-identified: the Newtonian equation normalizes away distance dependence and lacks a step size or class-size normalization.
Reviewer-identified: the relativity algorithm neither learns a manifold metric nor calculates a geodesic.
Reviewer-identified: arbitrary feature scaling changes the relationship to the Schwarzschild radius and can enter singular or non-real update regions.
Reviewer-identified: the Minkowski update ignores the Cartesian direction to the attracting sample.
Reviewer-identified: one small in-sample dataset and qualitative plots cannot establish accuracy, generalization, robustness, or scalability.
Reviewer-identified: no standard supervised DR, metric-learning, force-directed embedding, or simple centroid-shrinkage baseline is evaluated.
Reviewer-identified: no objective, convergence definition, stability argument, complexity analysis, runtime result, or memory result is provided.
Reviewer-identified: independently recomputed t-SNE plots can change layout between iterations and are not a controlled quantitative comparison.
Reviewer-identified: the method intentionally erases within-class geometry, but preservation of modes, neighborhoods, density, fairness, and rare subpopulations is not evaluated.
Reviewer-identified: label noise, imbalance, noncontiguous label encodings, small classes, duplicate points, and singular coordinates are untested.
Reviewer-identified: the public code makes undocumented choices for iteration count and singular radial updates and has no automated empirical test suite.
failure_modes: No learning rate means the sum of many unit pair forces can overshoot, oscillate, or grow with class cardinality.
Coincident or nearly coincident points create divisions by zero or unstable inverse-distance terms.
Schwarzschild updates become singular at r=2, non-real under the stated square root for r<2, and singular on spherical-coordinate axes.
Rescaling features or changing PCA normalization can qualitatively switch the relativity branch between regular and singular regimes.
Minkowski steps can drift all classes toward negative coordinate directions instead of their attracting points.
Sequential in-place updates can make results depend on ties or instability in the LOF ordering.
Small classes can make fixed-neighbor LOF ill-posed or trigger implementation adjustments not modeled by the paper.
Noisy labels can pull semantically unrelated points into an artificial compact cluster and hide annotation errors.
Multimodal classes can collapse distinct subtypes, trajectories, or rare groups that are important downstream.
Class imbalance can give points in large classes much larger aggregate displacement than points in small classes.
Applying the contraction jointly to train and test data would leak test labels and test-set geometry.
A transform learned only as moved training coordinates cannot embed a genuinely new sample without an additional model.
t-SNE can make label-conditioned contraction look persuasive even when held-out classification or neighborhood preservation worsens.
Quadratic within-class pair interactions can become prohibitive as sample counts grow.
reusable_insights: Algebraically simplify a physics-inspired update before interpreting it; normalization can remove the physical dependence the notation appears to retain.
Separate a physical metaphor from the actual optimization rule and evaluate the rule against simpler non-physical baselines.
A claimed geodesic method should define a global or learned metric and solve or accurately discretize the geodesic equations.
Nondimensionalize coordinates and test invariance to feature units before importing constants or singular radii from physics.
Supervised embeddings need an explicit held-out protocol and a label-free transform for new samples.
Measure both class utility and structural damage with held-out classification, trustworthiness, continuity, neighborhood recall, density preservation, and subgroup metrics.
Use centroid shrinkage, NCA, LMNN, supervised UMAP, ClassNeRV, and a plain force-directed objective as causal baselines.
Define an objective, stopping criterion, damping schedule, and numerical safeguards for iterative attraction methods.
Report fixed-seed or aligned embedding comparisons instead of treating separately optimized t-SNE pictures as quantitative evidence.
Stress-test label noise, class imbalance, multimodal classes, duplicate samples, arbitrary rescaling, and out-of-distribution inputs.
When within-class collapse is the intended signal, quantify which fine-grained information remains recoverable rather than assuming all within-class variance is nuisance.
open_questions: Does any GDR variant improve held-out classifier accuracy over PCA, LDA, NCA, LMNN, supervised UMAP, and simple centroid shrinkage?
Can a mathematically defined energy make the updates monotone and yield a convergence or stability guarantee?
What remains of the claimed Newtonian advantage after recognizing that every pair contributes a unit vector?
Can the relativity variant be reformulated with a learned Riemannian metric and an actual geodesic integrator?
How should the Schwarzschild radius and physical constants be nondimensionalized so results are invariant to feature units?
What numerical behavior occurs near r=0, r=2, polar axes, duplicate samples, and very small classes?
Can a parametric or kernel extension embed new unlabeled points without using test labels or test geometry?
How much neighborhood, density, subtype, and rare-group information is destroyed as class scatter contracts?
Are the visual gains reproducible with a fixed downstream embedding, seeds, aligned coordinates, and quantitative quality metrics?
How do runtime and memory scale with number of samples, class imbalance, and input dimension?
Is density sorting beneficial after controlling for random order, centroid order, and parallel batch updates?
Would attractive and repulsive forces between same- and different-class neighbors avoid total class collapse and yield a better metric-learning objective?

competitive_landscape.title: Neighbourhood Components Analysis
competitive_landscape.difference: NCA directly optimizes a stochastic leave-one-out nearest-neighbor objective and learns an explicit low-rank linear transform, with quantitative comparisons and out-of-sample projection. GDR instead moves the labeled training samples themselves, has no predictive objective or inductive map, and does not compare against NCA.

competitive_landscape.title: Distance Metric Learning for Large Margin Nearest Neighbor Classification
competitive_landscape.difference: LMNN learns a positive semidefinite Mahalanobis metric that pulls target neighbors together while separating impostors by a margin and evaluates held-out kNN accuracy across datasets. GDR has only within-class attraction, no between-class margin, no learned test-time metric, and no held-out evaluation.

competitive_landscape.title: Joint Dimensionality Reduction and Metric Learning: A Geometric Take
competitive_landscape.difference: DRML learns a low-dimensional mapping and metric jointly on a Riemannian optimization domain, reporting runtime and predictive accuracy against major metric-learning baselines. GDR uses geometry terminology but fixes PCA to three dimensions, does not learn the metric tensor, and supplies neither a joint objective nor quantitative comparisons.

competitive_landscape.title: UMAP: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection for Dimension Reduction
competitive_landscape.difference: UMAP defines attractive and repulsive neighborhood objectives from an explicit manifold-learning construction, scales to real datasets, supports general embedding dimensions, and has supervised and transform extensions in its implementation lineage. GDR uses only same-class attraction and can manufacture separation by destroying intra-class geometry, without measuring neighborhood preservation or out-of-sample quality.

competitive_landscape.title: Steering Distortions to Preserve Classes and Neighbors in Supervised Dimensionality Reduction
competitive_landscape.difference: ClassNeRV explicitly balances class separation against false- and missed-neighbor distortions and compares against nine alternatives. That tradeoff directly addresses GDR's unmeasured destruction of within-class structure; GDR optimizes contraction alone and offers no neighbor-preservation control.

competitive_landscape.title: Force2Vec: Parallel force-directed graph embedding
competitive_landscape.difference: Force2Vec operationalizes attractive and repulsive layout forces as a graph-embedding objective, maps computation to parallel linear algebra, reports up to billion-edge scaling, and evaluates visualization plus downstream tasks. It demonstrates that physical-force-inspired embeddings predate GDR and that such an analogy can be paired with scalability and quantitative validation.

competitive_landscape.title: Enhancing Supervised Visualization through Autoencoder and Random Forest Proximities for Out-of-Sample Extension
competitive_landscape.difference: This RF-PHATE extension uses an autoencoder to learn a label-free map for unseen points, quantitatively evaluates alternative reconstruction targets, and reports consistent quality using a subset of training data. It directly addresses the out-of-sample limitation GDR leaves as future work.

competitive_landscape.title: Gradient Boosting Mapping for Dimensionality Reduction and Feature Extraction
competitive_landscape.difference: GBMAP learns explicit low-dimensional supervised features from simple weak learners, evaluates prediction and distance quality, detects distribution shift, and reports million-sample timing. It is a current alternative when the goal is discriminative, human-inspectable coordinates rather than transductive collapse of labeled samples.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim a novel hybrid of physics and machine learning that performs supervised dimensionality reduction through Newtonian attraction or motion along general- and special-relativistic geodesics, using Schwarzschild and Minkowski metrics to separate classes.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper specifies sequential within-class update rules, releases a Python implementation, and shows visually compacted label-colored groups on one digits dataset across Newtonian, Schwarzschild, Minkowski, and coordinate-weight variants.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The narrow novelty is a particular set of physics-themed coordinate updates for label-conditioned sample contraction. The Newtonian rule algebraically reduces to summed unit directions, the Minkowski rule lacks attraction direction, and the Schwarzschild rule neither learns geometry nor follows geodesics and has scale-dependent singularities. Supervised metric learning, class-aware visualization, joint geometric DR, and force-directed embeddings are substantial prior fields with explicit objectives, inductive transforms, preservation tradeoffs, and quantitative evaluation. The physical interpretation and broad dimensionality-reduction claim are therefore not established; the paper is best treated as an unvalidated visualization heuristic requiring mathematical repair before empirical comparison.

reviewer_notes: Read all 14 cached pages and visually inspected every experiment panel in Figures 1-3. Algebraically checked the Newtonian and Minkowski equations and traced the Schwarzschild singularities through Algorithms 1-3. Also inspected the linked author repository at commit 848a8d08cc8dc3da6bb54d81cccf0a45d7eed36f (latest commit dated 2022-11-10), including GDR.py and main.py; no experiments were rerun. verification.competitor_check: Checked primary records for NCA in the NIPS 2004 proceedings, LMNN in JMLR 10, DRML in PMLR 70, ClassNeRV in NeurIPS 2020, arXiv:1802.03426v3, arXiv:2009.10035v1, arXiv:2406.04421v1, and arXiv:2405.08486v1. The panel covers supervised metric learning, joint geometric DR, class-versus-neighborhood tradeoffs, scalable neighbor and force embeddings, inductive out-of-sample extension, and current supervised feature maps.
